title: Closed-image exceptional components detect stability
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed $T$-curve with smooth $X_\eta$ and etale $D_\eta$. Let $f:(Y,E)\to(X,D)$ be a semistable $\eta$-modification. Write $B_f$ for the set of points $z\in Y$ such that, for some $t\in T$, $z$ is the generic point (its closure is the whole component) of an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] $C_z$ of $Y_t$, and $f_Y(z)$ is a closed point of the entire scheme $X$, not merely of $X_t$. Call $z$ exceptional if $f_Y$ contracts $C_z$ to a point and, after base change to an algebraic closure of $\kappa(t)$, $C_z$ is $\mathbf P^1$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of the fibre in at most two points. Then $B_f$ is finite, and $f$ is stable if and only if no element of $B_f$ is exceptional. In particular, if $f$ is not stable, some exceptional $z$ belongs to $B_f$. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

proof.text: The set $T$ is finite by the finite-chain hypothesis. Finite presentation of $Y\to T$ implies finite type: on affine charts its algebra has finitely many generators, and the morphism is quasi-compact. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2), each fibre $Y_t$ is of finite type over $\kappa(t)$. The spectrum of a field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are zero and the whole field. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Y_t$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] makes its component set finite. A scheme has at most one generic point for each irreducible closed subset (on any common affine neighbourhood equality of the closures gives equality of the corresponding prime ideals). Thus there are finitely many fibre-component generic points over the finite set $T$, and $B_f$, being a subset, is finite. This uses neither properness nor separatedness of $X\to T$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2 finiteness, printed pp. 26--27; Stacks Tags 01T4, 01T6 and 0BA8

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-semistable-normal-target-factorization] to the given $f$. It supplies a normal multipointed $T$-curve $(N,D_N)$ with smooth generic curve and etale generic marking, and a semistable $\eta$-modification $g:(Y,E)\to(N,D_N)$ with $f=\nu\circ g$. Its component-contraction equivalence, on both ordinary and geometric fibres, shows that $f$ and $g$ have exactly the same exceptional components: the projective-line and special-point conditions use only the unchanged source $(Y,E)$. Thus if $f$ is not stable then $g$ is not stable. Keep $B_f$ and closedness relative to the original target $X$; no assertion that $X$ itself is normal is made.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4, first sentence, printed p. 31: normalization reduction with marking and contraction compatibility made explicit.

proof.text: Assume $f$ is not stable. By step 2, $g$ is not stable, so it has an exceptional component in a geometric fibre over some $s\in T$. The finite-type fibre $Y_s$ has pure one-dimensional geometric fibres with only smooth points or ordinary nodes, by semistability. Hence [lem-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres-reduced] makes it geometrically reduced. Apply [lem-trf-sepclosed-valuation-geometric-components] to $Y_s$. It identifies that geometric component with $C_{\overline{\kappa(s)}}$ for a unique irreducible component $C\subseteq Y_s$. Its image under $g_Y$ is a point, since the field-extension projection is surjective and its composite image is a point. The projective-line and geometric special-point conditions are unchanged. Thus $C$ is exceptional for $g$. Write $z$ for its generic point and $W=\overline{\{z\}}\subseteq Y$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4, choice of an exceptional component, printed p. 31; geometric-component interpretation

proof.text: The image $I$ of $W\to T$ is a nonempty subset of the finite chain $T$. Choose its most special point $t$. Every point of $W$ is a specialization of $z$, so $t$ is a specialization of $s$. The singleton $\{t\}$ is closed in $I$: in an affine spectrum closure means containment of prime ideals, and maximality within $I$ leaves no other specialization. Therefore $W_t$ is nonempty and closed in $W$, hence closed in $Y$. This does not assert that $t$ is the closed point of the whole valuation spectrum; $I$ can omit that point.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2 proof, choice of the closed point of the image of the component closure, printed p. 27

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-exceptional-component-specialization] to $g:(Y,E)\to(N,D_N)$ and to $C,W,t$. Step 2 supplies normality of $N$, smooth generic curve, etale generic marking and the semistable modification; steps 3--4 give the exceptional $C$, the specialization $t$ and nonempty $W_t$. We obtain an exceptional component $C_t$ of $Y_t$ contained in $W_t$. By [def-weil-irreducible-components], $C_t$ is closed in $Y_t$, hence closed in $W_t$ and then in $Y$. The contraction equivalence of [lem-trf-semistable-normal-target-factorization] gives $f_Y(C_t)=\{x\}$; its projective-line and special-point conditions are the same for $f$ and $g$. By [def-weil-proper-morphism], the original proper $f_Y:Y\to X$ is closed, so this singleton is closed in the entire $X$. The generic point $z_t$ of $C_t$ therefore belongs to $B_f$ and is exceptional for $f$.

source.place: Lemmas 4.2.2 and 4.4.4, printed pp. 26--27 and 31--32, AFTER normalization; original proper map used for closedness in X.

proof.text: The component correspondence of [lem-trf-sepclosed-valuation-geometric-components], applicable to each nodal fibre by [lem-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres-reduced] as in step 3, identifies the ordinary exceptional components in the statement with geometric exceptional components. If $f$ is stable, no geometric fibre has an exceptional component, so no element of $B_f$ is exceptional. Conversely, if no element of $B_f$ is exceptional but $f$ were not stable, step 5 would supply such an element, a contradiction. Combined with step 1 this proves finiteness, the equivalence, and its stated particular consequence.

lean.statement: theorem valuation_exceptional_closed_image_criterion (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsSepClosed K] (V : ValuationSubring K) [Finite (PrimeSpectrum V)] (X Y : MultipointedCurve (Spec (.of V))) (hX : Smooth (pullback.snd X.x (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype)))) (hD : Etale (pullback.snd X.d (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype)))) (f : Y.Hom X) (hf : f.IsEtaModification (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype))) (hY : Y.IsSemistable) : f.closedImageFiberGenericPoints.Finite ∧ (f.IsStable (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype)) ↔ ∀ z ∈ f.closedImageFiberGenericPoints, ¬ f.IsExceptionalFiberGenericPoint z) ∧ (¬ f.IsStable (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype)) → ∃ z ∈ f.closedImageFiberGenericPoints, f.IsExceptionalFiberGenericPoint z)
